title: Check if All A's Appears Before All B's
statement: The string `s` is made only of the letters `'a'` and `'b'`. Return `true` when no `'a'` sits at a later position than some `'b'` (in other words, all of the `'a'`s come first and all of the `'b'`s after them), and `false` otherwise. A string with no `'a'` or no `'b'` at all counts as `true`.
constraints: s contains only the characters 'a' and 'b'
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every pair of positions for a `'b'` followed later by an `'a'` works in O(n²), but one left-to-right pass is enough. The string fails exactly when some `'a'` shows up after a `'b'` has already been read, so it suffices to remember whether a `'b'` has appeared yet. (Equivalently, the string fails exactly when it contains `"ba"`.)

## Approach

1. Start with `seenB = false`.
2. Read the characters `ch` of `s` in order.
3. If `ch` is `'b'`, set `seenB` to `true`.
4. Otherwise `ch` is `'a'`; if `seenB` is already `true`, this `'a'` comes after a `'b'`, so return `false`.
5. If the loop finishes, every `'a'` came before every `'b'`: return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "aaabbb"`. The first three characters are `'a'` while `seenB` is still `false`, so nothing happens. The fourth character is `'b'` and sets `seenB = true`; the last two are also `'b'`. No `'a'` arrives after that, so the loop ends and the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is read once.
- Space: O(1): one boolean flag.

## Pitfalls

- Strings with only `'a'`s or only `'b'`s are valid and must return `true`.
- Do not compare counts or check only the first and last characters: `"abab"` starts with `'a'` and ends with `'b'` yet fails.
- Return `false` as soon as the violation appears; the rest of the string cannot fix it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seenB` | whether a `'b'` has been read so far |
| `ch` | the current character |

narration.3: Read the characters from left to right.
narration.5: Remember that a 'b' has appeared; any later 'a' would break the order.
narration.6: Otherwise it is an 'a': has a 'b' already appeared before it?
narration.7: Yes, so this 'a' comes after a 'b' and the answer is false.
narration.10: No 'a' came after a 'b', so every 'a' is before every 'b'.
